text: term: hello ¦ reading: /həˈloʊ/ ¦ part_of_speech: phrase ¦ meaning: en: a friendly greeting | ar: مرحبًا ¦ example: Hello, my name is Sara. ¦ example_meaning: en: Hello, my name is Sara. | ar: مرحبًا، اسمي سارة.

term: good morning ¦ reading: /ɡʊd ˈmɔːrnɪŋ/ ¦ part_of_speech: phrase ¦ meaning: en: greeting used before noon | ar: صباح الخير ¦ example: Good morning! How are you? ¦ example_meaning: en: Good morning! How are you? | ar: صباح الخير! كيف حالك؟

term: thank you ¦ reading: /ˈθæŋk juː/ ¦ part_of_speech: phrase ¦ meaning: en: words to show gratitude | ar: شكرًا لك ¦ example: Thank you for your help. ¦ example_meaning: en: Thank you for your help. | ar: شكرًا لك على مساعدتك.

term: please ¦ reading: /pliːz/ ¦ part_of_speech: adverb ¦ meaning: en: a polite word used when asking | ar: من فضلك ¦ example: A glass of water, please. ¦ example_meaning: en: A glass of water, please. | ar: كوب ماء من فضلك.
term: sorry ¦ reading: /ˈsɑːri/ ¦ part_of_speech: adjective ¦ meaning: en: used to apologise | ar: آسف ¦ example: Sorry, I'm late. ¦ example_meaning: en: Sorry, I'm late. | ar: آسف، لقد تأخرت.

term: goodbye ¦ reading: /ɡʊdˈbaɪ/ ¦ part_of_speech: phrase ¦ meaning: en: said when leaving | ar: مع السلامة ¦ example: Goodbye, see you tomorrow. ¦ example_meaning: en: Goodbye, see you tomorrow. | ar: مع السلامة، أراك غدًا.
term: name ¦ reading: /neɪm/ ¦ part_of_speech: noun ¦ meaning: en: the word you are called by | ar: اسم ¦ example: What is your name? ¦ example_meaning: en: What is your name? | ar: ما اسمك؟

term: nice to meet you ¦ reading: /naɪs tə miːt juː/ ¦ part_of_speech: phrase ¦ meaning: en: said when meeting someone for the first time | ar: تشرّفت بمعرفتك ¦ example: I'm Omar. Nice to meet you. ¦ example_meaning: en: I'm Omar. Nice to meet you. | ar: أنا عمر. تشرّفت بمعرفتك.

term: family ¦ reading: /ˈfæməli/ ¦ part_of_speech: noun ¦ meaning: en: parents, children, brothers and sisters | ar: عائلة ¦ example: My family lives in Amman. ¦ example_meaning: en: My family lives in Amman. | ar: تعيش عائلتي في عمّان.
term: mother ¦ reading: /ˈmʌðər/ ¦ part_of_speech: noun ¦ meaning: en: female parent | ar: أم
term: father ¦ reading: /ˈfɑːðər/ ¦ part_of_speech: noun ¦ meaning: en: male parent | ar: أب
term: brother ¦ reading: /ˈbrʌðər/ ¦ part_of_speech: noun ¦ meaning: en: a male sibling | ar: أخ
term: sister ¦ reading: /ˈsɪstər/ ¦ part_of_speech: noun ¦ meaning: en: a female sibling | ar: أخت

term: friend ¦ reading: /frend/ ¦ part_of_speech: noun ¦ meaning: en: a person you like and know well | ar: صديق ¦ example: She is my best friend. ¦ example_meaning: en: She is my best friend. | ar: هي أعزّ صديقاتي.
term: water ¦ reading: /ˈwɔːtər/ ¦ part_of_speech: noun ¦ meaning: en: the clear liquid we drink | ar: ماء

term: coffee ¦ reading: /ˈkɔːfi/ ¦ part_of_speech: noun ¦ meaning: en: a hot brown drink | ar: قهوة ¦ example: I'd like a coffee, please. ¦ example_meaning: en: I'd like a coffee, please. | ar: أريد قهوة من فضلك.
term: tea ¦ reading: /tiː/ ¦ part_of_speech: noun ¦ meaning: en: a hot drink made from leaves | ar: شاي
term: bread ¦ reading: /bred/ ¦ part_of_speech: noun ¦ meaning: en: food made from flour and baked | ar: خبز

term: menu ¦ reading: /ˈmenjuː/ ¦ part_of_speech: noun ¦ meaning: en: a list of food in a restaurant | ar: قائمة الطعام ¦ example: Can I see the menu, please? ¦ example_meaning: en: Can I see the menu, please? | ar: هل يمكنني رؤية قائمة الطعام من فضلك؟

term: the bill ¦ reading: /bɪl/ ¦ part_of_speech: noun ¦ meaning: en: the paper showing how much to pay in a restaurant | ar: الحساب (الفاتورة) ¦ example: Could we have the bill, please? ¦ example_meaning: en: Could we have the bill, please? | ar: هل يمكننا الحصول على الحساب من فضلك؟
term: hungry ¦ reading: /ˈhʌŋɡri/ ¦ part_of_speech: adjective ¦ meaning: en: wanting to eat | ar: جائع
term: today ¦ reading: /təˈdeɪ/ ¦ part_of_speech: adverb ¦ meaning: en: this day | ar: اليوم
term: tomorrow ¦ reading: /təˈmɑːroʊ/ ¦ part_of_speech: adverb ¦ meaning: en: the day after today | ar: غدًا
term: yesterday ¦ reading: /ˈjestərdeɪ/ ¦ part_of_speech: adverb ¦ meaning: en: the day before today | ar: أمس
term: morning ¦ reading: /ˈmɔːrnɪŋ/ ¦ part_of_speech: noun ¦ meaning: en: the early part of the day | ar: صباح
term: evening ¦ reading: /ˈiːvnɪŋ/ ¦ part_of_speech: noun ¦ meaning: en: the end of the day, before night | ar: مساء
term: week ¦ reading: /wiːk/ ¦ part_of_speech: noun ¦ meaning: en: seven days | ar: أسبوع

term: station ¦ reading: /ˈsteɪʃən/ ¦ part_of_speech: noun ¦ meaning: en: a place where trains or buses stop | ar: محطة ¦ example: Where is the train station? ¦ example_meaning: en: Where is the train station? | ar: أين محطة القطار؟

term: ticket ¦ reading: /ˈtɪkɪt/ ¦ part_of_speech: noun ¦ meaning: en: a paper that lets you travel or enter | ar: تذكرة ¦ example: One ticket to London, please. ¦ example_meaning: en: One ticket to London, please. | ar: تذكرة واحدة إلى لندن من فضلك.
term: left ¦ reading: /left/ ¦ part_of_speech: noun ¦ meaning: en: the opposite of right (direction) | ar: يسار
term: right ¦ reading: /raɪt/ ¦ part_of_speech: noun ¦ meaning: en: the opposite of left (direction) | ar: يمين

term: straight on ¦ reading: /streɪt ɒn/ ¦ part_of_speech: phrase ¦ meaning: en: forward without turning | ar: إلى الأمام مباشرة ¦ example: Go straight on and turn left. ¦ example_meaning: en: Go straight on and turn left. | ar: امشِ إلى الأمام مباشرة ثم انعطف يسارًا.
term: airport ¦ reading: /ˈerpɔːrt/ ¦ part_of_speech: noun ¦ meaning: en: a place where planes take off and land | ar: مطار
term: hotel ¦ reading: /hoʊˈtel/ ¦ part_of_speech: noun ¦ meaning: en: a building where you pay to stay | ar: فندق

term: wake up ¦ reading: /weɪk ʌp/ ¦ part_of_speech: verb ¦ meaning: en: to stop sleeping | ar: يستيقظ ¦ example: I wake up at seven. ¦ example_meaning: en: I wake up at seven. | ar: أستيقظ في السابعة.
term: work ¦ reading: /wɜːrk/ ¦ part_of_speech: verb ¦ meaning: en: to do a job | ar: يعمل

term: study ¦ reading: /ˈstʌdi/ ¦ part_of_speech: verb ¦ meaning: en: to learn about a subject | ar: يدرس ¦ example: I study English every day. ¦ example_meaning: en: I study English every day. | ar: أدرس الإنجليزية كل يوم.

term: usually ¦ reading: /ˈjuːʒuəli/ ¦ part_of_speech: adverb ¦ meaning: en: most of the time | ar: عادةً ¦ example: I usually drink tea in the morning. ¦ example_meaning: en: I usually drink tea in the morning. | ar: عادةً أشرب الشاي في الصباح.
term: busy ¦ reading: /ˈbɪzi/ ¦ part_of_speech: adjective ¦ meaning: en: having a lot to do | ar: مشغول
term: happy ¦ reading: /ˈhæpi/ ¦ part_of_speech: adjective ¦ meaning: en: feeling good and pleased | ar: سعيد
term: tired ¦ reading: /ˈtaɪərd/ ¦ part_of_speech: adjective ¦ meaning: en: needing rest or sleep | ar: متعب
term: worried ¦ reading: /ˈwɜːrid/ ¦ part_of_speech: adjective ¦ meaning: en: unhappy because you think something bad may happen | ar: قلق

term: I think ¦ reading: /aɪ θɪŋk/ ¦ part_of_speech: phrase ¦ meaning: en: used to give your opinion | ar: أعتقد / في رأيي ¦ example: I think this book is interesting. ¦ example_meaning: en: I think this book is interesting. | ar: أعتقد أن هذا الكتاب ممتع.

term: although ¦ reading: /ɔːlˈðoʊ/ ¦ part_of_speech: conjunction ¦ meaning: en: despite the fact that | ar: على الرغم من أن ¦ example: Although it was raining, we went out. ¦ example_meaning: en: Although it was raining, we went out. | ar: على الرغم من أن المطر كان يهطل، خرجنا.

term: meeting ¦ reading: /ˈmiːtɪŋ/ ¦ part_of_speech: noun ¦ meaning: en: when people come together to discuss something | ar: اجتماع ¦ example: The meeting starts at ten. ¦ example_meaning: en: The meeting starts at ten. | ar: يبدأ الاجتماع في العاشرة.

term: deadline ¦ reading: /ˈdedlaɪn/ ¦ part_of_speech: noun ¦ meaning: en: the time by which something must be finished | ar: الموعد النهائي ¦ example: The deadline for the report is Friday. ¦ example_meaning: en: The deadline for the report is Friday. | ar: الموعد النهائي للتقرير هو الجمعة.
term: experience ¦ reading: /ɪkˈspɪriəns/ ¦ part_of_speech: noun ¦ meaning: en: knowledge or skill you get from doing something | ar: خبرة

term: improve ¦ reading: /ɪmˈpruːv/ ¦ part_of_speech: verb ¦ meaning: en: to become or make better | ar: يحسّن / يتحسّن ¦ example: I want to improve my speaking. ¦ example_meaning: en: I want to improve my speaking. | ar: أريد أن أحسّن مهارة التحدث لديّ.
term: schedule ¦ reading: /ˈskedʒuːl/ ¦ part_of_speech: noun ¦ meaning: en: a plan of when things will happen | ar: جدول زمني

term: achieve ¦ reading: /əˈtʃiːv/ ¦ part_of_speech: verb ¦ meaning: en: to succeed in doing something after effort | ar: يحقّق ¦ example: She achieved her goal of running a marathon. ¦ example_meaning: en: She achieved her goal of running a marathon. | ar: حقّقت هدفها بالركض في ماراثون.

term: how much ¦ reading: /haʊ mʌtʃ/ ¦ part_of_speech: phrase ¦ meaning: en: used to ask the price | ar: بكم / كم السعر ¦ example: How much is this shirt? ¦ example_meaning: en: How much is this shirt? | ar: بكم هذا القميص؟
term: cheap ¦ reading: /tʃiːp/ ¦ part_of_speech: adjective ¦ meaning: en: not costing much money | ar: رخيص
term: expensive ¦ reading: /ɪkˈspensɪv/ ¦ part_of_speech: adjective ¦ meaning: en: costing a lot of money | ar: غالٍ
term: size ¦ reading: /saɪz/ ¦ part_of_speech: noun ¦ meaning: en: how big or small something is | ar: مقاس / حجم

term: plan ¦ reading: /plæn/ ¦ part_of_speech: noun ¦ meaning: en: something you intend to do | ar: خطة ¦ example: What are your plans for the summer? ¦ example_meaning: en: What are your plans for the summer? | ar: ما خططك للصيف؟
term: be going to ¦ part_of_speech: phrase ¦ meaning: en: used for plans you have already decided | ar: ينوي / سوف (لخطة مقرّرة)
term: probably ¦ reading: /ˈprɒbəbli/ ¦ part_of_speech: adverb ¦ meaning: en: very likely | ar: على الأرجح
term: abroad ¦ reading: /əˈbrɔːd/ ¦ part_of_speech: adverb ¦ meaning: en: in or to another country | ar: في الخارج
term: save (money) ¦ part_of_speech: verb ¦ meaning: en: to keep money instead of spending it | ar: يدّخر (المال)
term: decide ¦ reading: /dɪˈsaɪd/ ¦ part_of_speech: verb ¦ meaning: en: to make a choice | ar: يقرّر

term: unless ¦ reading: /ənˈles/ ¦ part_of_speech: conjunction ¦ meaning: en: except if | ar: ما لم / إلا إذا ¦ example: I won't go unless you come too. ¦ example_meaning: en: I won't go unless you come too. | ar: لن أذهب إلا إذا أتيت أنت أيضًا.
term: afford ¦ reading: /əˈfɔːd/ ¦ part_of_speech: verb ¦ meaning: en: to have enough money for something | ar: يقدر على تحمّل تكلفة
term: opportunity ¦ reading: /ˌɒpəˈtjuːnəti/ ¦ part_of_speech: noun ¦ meaning: en: a chance to do something | ar: فرصة

term: regret ¦ reading: /rɪˈɡret/ ¦ part_of_speech: verb ¦ meaning: en: to feel sorry about something you did | ar: يندم

term: I don't understand. ¦ part_of_speech: phrase ¦ meaning: en: used when you can't follow what was said | ar: لا أفهم.

term: Where are the toilets? ¦ part_of_speech: phrase ¦ meaning: en: asking where the toilets are | ar: أين دورات المياه؟
term: Can you help me? ¦ part_of_speech: phrase ¦ meaning: en: asking for help | ar: هل يمكنك مساعدتي؟
term: I don't know. ¦ part_of_speech: phrase ¦ meaning: en: saying you have no information | ar: لا أعرف.
term: No problem. ¦ part_of_speech: phrase ¦ meaning: en: a friendly reply meaning 'it's fine' | ar: لا مشكلة.
term: Help! ¦ part_of_speech: phrase ¦ meaning: en: shouted when you are in danger | ar: النجدة!

term: Call an ambulance! ¦ part_of_speech: phrase ¦ meaning: en: asking someone to call medical help | ar: اتصل بالإسعاف! ¦ example: Please call an ambulance, he's hurt! ¦ example_meaning: en: Please call an ambulance, he's hurt! | ar: اتصل بالإسعاف من فضلك، إنه مصاب!

term: My bag has been stolen. ¦ part_of_speech: phrase ¦ meaning: en: reporting a theft | ar: سُرقت حقيبتي.
term: embassy ¦ part_of_speech: noun ¦ meaning: en: your country's official office abroad | ar: السفارة
term: hospital ¦ part_of_speech: noun ¦ meaning: en: a place where sick people are treated | ar: المستشفى
term: emergency number ¦ part_of_speech: noun ¦ meaning: en: the phone number for police, fire or ambulance | ar: رقم الطوارئ

term: A table for two, please. ¦ part_of_speech: phrase ¦ meaning: en: asking for a table | ar: طاولة لشخصين من فضلك. ¦ example: Good evening. A table for two, please. ¦ example_meaning: en: Good evening. A table for two, please. | ar: مساء الخير. طاولة لشخصين من فضلك.
term: What do you recommend? ¦ part_of_speech: phrase ¦ meaning: en: asking for a suggestion | ar: بماذا تنصحني؟

term: starter ¦ part_of_speech: noun ¦ meaning: en: a small first dish | ar: المقبّلات
term: main course ¦ part_of_speech: noun ¦ meaning: en: the biggest dish of a meal | ar: الطبق الرئيسي
term: dessert ¦ part_of_speech: noun ¦ meaning: en: sweet food at the end of a meal | ar: الحلوى
term: tip ¦ part_of_speech: noun ¦ meaning: en: extra money you give for good service | ar: البقشيش

term: reservation ¦ part_of_speech: noun ¦ meaning: en: an arrangement to keep a room or table for you | ar: حجز ¦ example: I have a reservation under the name Hassan. ¦ example_meaning: en: I have a reservation under the name Hassan. | ar: لديّ حجز باسم حسن.
term: check in ¦ part_of_speech: verb ¦ meaning: en: to arrive and register at a hotel | ar: تسجيل الوصول
term: check out ¦ part_of_speech: verb ¦ meaning: en: to pay and leave a hotel | ar: تسجيل المغادرة
term: single room ¦ part_of_speech: noun ¦ meaning: en: a room for one person | ar: غرفة لشخص واحد
term: double room ¦ part_of_speech: noun ¦ meaning: en: a room for two people | ar: غرفة لشخصين (مزدوجة)
term: key ¦ part_of_speech: noun ¦ meaning: en: a small object that opens a door | ar: مفتاح

term: What's the Wi-Fi password? ¦ part_of_speech: phrase ¦ meaning: en: asking how to connect to the internet | ar: ما كلمة مرور الواي فاي؟

term: return ticket ¦ part_of_speech: noun ¦ meaning: en: a ticket to go and come back | ar: تذكرة ذهاب وعودة
term: single ticket ¦ part_of_speech: noun ¦ meaning: en: a ticket for one direction | ar: تذكرة ذهاب فقط
term: departure ¦ part_of_speech: noun ¦ meaning: en: leaving; the time a train or plane leaves | ar: المغادرة
term: delayed ¦ part_of_speech: adjective ¦ meaning: en: later than planned | ar: متأخر
term: boarding pass ¦ part_of_speech: noun ¦ meaning: en: the card you need to get on a plane | ar: بطاقة الصعود إلى الطائرة
term: luggage ¦ part_of_speech: noun ¦ meaning: en: the bags you travel with | ar: الأمتعة
term: bus stop ¦ part_of_speech: noun ¦ meaning: en: where a bus stops for passengers | ar: موقف الحافلات

term: museum ¦ part_of_speech: noun ¦ meaning: en: a building where art or history is shown | ar: متحف ¦ example: What time does the museum open? ¦ example_meaning: en: What time does the museum open? | ar: متى يفتح المتحف؟
term: opening hours ¦ part_of_speech: noun ¦ meaning: en: the times a place is open | ar: مواعيد العمل
term: entrance fee ¦ part_of_speech: noun ¦ meaning: en: money you pay to go in | ar: رسم الدخول
term: guided tour ¦ part_of_speech: noun ¦ meaning: en: a visit with a guide who explains | ar: جولة مع مرشد
term: map ¦ part_of_speech: noun ¦ meaning: en: a drawing of an area that shows the way | ar: خريطة

term: old town ¦ part_of_speech: noun ¦ meaning: en: the historic centre of a city | ar: المدينة القديمة
term: souvenir ¦ part_of_speech: noun ¦ meaning: en: something you buy to remember a trip | ar: تذكار

term: suddenly ¦ reading: /ˈsʌdənli/ ¦ part_of_speech: adverb ¦ meaning: en: quickly and unexpectedly | ar: فجأة ¦ example: Suddenly the lights went out. ¦ example_meaning: en: Suddenly the lights went out. | ar: فجأة انطفأت الأضواء.

term: happen ¦ reading: /ˈhæpən/ ¦ part_of_speech: verb ¦ meaning: en: to take place | ar: يحدث ¦ example: What happened after the party? ¦ example_meaning: en: What happened after the party? | ar: ماذا حدث بعد الحفلة؟

term: while ¦ reading: /waɪl/ ¦ part_of_speech: conjunction ¦ meaning: en: during the time that | ar: بينما ¦ example: I was cooking while she was reading. ¦ example_meaning: en: I was cooking while she was reading. | ar: كنت أطبخ بينما كانت تقرأ.
term: notice ¦ reading: /ˈnoʊtɪs/ ¦ part_of_speech: verb ¦ meaning: en: to see or become aware of something | ar: يلاحظ

term: accident ¦ reading: /ˈæksɪdənt/ ¦ part_of_speech: noun ¦ meaning: en: something bad that happens by chance | ar: حادث ¦ example: Nobody was hurt in the accident. ¦ example_meaning: en: Nobody was hurt in the accident. | ar: لم يُصب أحد في الحادث.
term: remember ¦ reading: /rɪˈmembər/ ¦ part_of_speech: verb ¦ meaning: en: to keep something in your mind | ar: يتذكّر

term: advice ¦ reading: /ədˈvaɪs/ ¦ part_of_speech: noun ¦ meaning: en: an opinion about what someone should do | ar: نصيحة ¦ example: Can I give you some advice? ¦ example_meaning: en: Can I give you some advice? | ar: هل يمكنني أن أقدّم لك نصيحة؟

term: be allowed to ¦ part_of_speech: phrase ¦ meaning: en: to have permission to do something | ar: يُسمح له بـ

term: recommend ¦ reading: /ˌrekəˈmend/ ¦ part_of_speech: verb ¦ meaning: en: to say that something is good or suitable | ar: يوصي بـ

term: neighbour ¦ reading: /ˈneɪbər/ ¦ part_of_speech: noun ¦ meaning: en: a person who lives near you | ar: جار ¦ example: My neighbour has a big dog. ¦ example_meaning: en: My neighbour has a big dog. | ar: لدى جاري كلب كبير.
term: colleague ¦ reading: /ˈkɒliːɡ/ ¦ part_of_speech: noun ¦ meaning: en: a person you work with | ar: زميل

title: en: The verb 'to be' | ar: فعل الكينونة 'to be' ¦ rule: en: Use am with I, is with he/she/it, and are with you/we/they. Arabic often omits 'to be' in the present, but English needs it. | ar: استخدم am مع I، وis مع he/she/it، وare مع you/we/they. كثيرًا ما تُحذف 'الكينونة' في العربية في المضارع، لكن الإنجليزية تحتاجها. ¦ examples: I am a student. = en: I am a student. | ar: أنا طالب. / She is a doctor. = en: She is a doctor. | ar: هي طبيبة. / They are friends. = en: They are friends. | ar: هم أصدقاء. / [marked incorrect] She doctor. = en: Missing 'is' | ar: ينقصها 'is' ¦ common_mistakes: en: Leaving out 'is': ✗ He happy → ✓ He is happy. | ar: حذف 'is': ✗ He happy ← ✓ He is happy. / en: Using 'is' with I: ✗ I is → ✓ I am. | ar: استخدام 'is' مع I: ✗ I is ← ✓ I am.

title: en: Polite requests: I'd like / Could I | ar: الطلب بأدب: I'd like / Could I ¦ rule: en: 'I'd like…' (I would like) is more polite than 'I want…'. Use 'Could I/we have…?' to ask for something. | ar: عبارة I'd like (أي I would like) أكثر تهذيبًا من I want. واستخدم Could I/we have…? للطلب. ¦ examples: I'd like a coffee, please. = en: I'd like a coffee, please. | ar: أريد قهوة من فضلك. / Could I have the menu? = en: Could I have the menu? | ar: هل يمكنني الحصول على القائمة؟ ¦ common_mistakes: en: 'Give me a coffee' can sound rude; prefer 'Could I have a coffee?'. | ar: قد تبدو عبارة Give me a coffee فظّة؛ الأفضل Could I have a coffee?

title: en: Present simple | ar: المضارع البسيط ¦ rule: en: Use the present simple for habits and facts. Add -s/-es to the verb after he, she or it. | ar: يُستخدم المضارع البسيط للعادات والحقائق. أضف ‎-s أو ‎-es للفعل بعد he وshe وit. ¦ examples: I work in an office. = en: I work in an office. | ar: أعمل في مكتب. / He works at night. = en: He works at night. | ar: يعمل ليلًا. / [marked incorrect] She work here. = en: Missing -s | ar: ينقصها ‎-s ¦ common_mistakes: en: Forgetting -s: ✗ She like tea → ✓ She likes tea. | ar: نسيان ‎-s: ✗ She like tea ← ✓ She likes tea. / en: Using 'is' with another verb: ✗ I am work → ✓ I work. | ar: استخدام is مع فعل آخر: ✗ I am work ← ✓ I work.

title: en: Imperatives for directions | ar: صيغة الأمر للاتجاهات ¦ rule: en: Give directions with the base verb: Go, Turn, Take. Add 'please' or 'Could you…' to be polite. | ar: أعطِ الاتجاهات بصيغة الفعل الأساسية: Go وTurn وTake. أضف please أو Could you… للتهذيب. ¦ examples: Turn right at the bank. = en: Turn right at the bank. | ar: انعطف يمينًا عند البنك. / Take the second street on the left. = en: Take the second street on the left. | ar: خذ الشارع الثاني على اليسار. ¦ common_mistakes: en: Adding 'to': ✗ To turn left → ✓ Turn left. | ar: إضافة to: ✗ To turn left ← ✓ Turn left.

title: en: Comparatives | ar: صيغ المقارنة ¦ rule: en: Short adjectives add -er (cheap → cheaper). Long adjectives use 'more' (expensive → more expensive). Use 'than' to compare. | ar: الصفات القصيرة تأخذ ‎-er ‏(cheap ← cheaper)، والطويلة تُسبق بـ more ‏(more expensive). واستخدم than للمقارنة. ¦ examples: This bag is cheaper than that one. = en: This bag is cheaper than that one. | ar: هذه الحقيبة أرخص من تلك. / This phone is more expensive. = en: This phone is more expensive. | ar: هذا الهاتف أغلى. / [marked incorrect] more cheaper = en: Double comparative | ar: مقارنة مزدوجة ¦ common_mistakes: en: Double comparison: ✗ more cheaper → ✓ cheaper. | ar: مقارنة مزدوجة: ✗ more cheaper ← ✓ cheaper.

title: en: Present perfect | ar: المضارع التام ¦ rule: en: have/has + past participle connects the past to now: experiences (I have been to Rome) and results (I have finished). | ar: have/has + التصريف الثالث يربط الماضي بالحاضر: للتجارب (I have been to Rome) وللنتائج (I have finished). ¦ examples: I have visited Cairo twice. = en: I have visited Cairo twice. | ar: زرت القاهرة مرتين. / She has finished the report. = en: She has finished the report. | ar: أنهت التقرير. / [marked incorrect] I have seen him yesterday. = en: Use past simple with 'yesterday' | ar: استخدم الماضي البسيط مع yesterday ¦ common_mistakes: en: Using it with a finished time: ✗ I have seen him yesterday → ✓ I saw him yesterday. | ar: استخدامه مع زمن منتهٍ: ✗ I have seen him yesterday ← ✓ I saw him yesterday.

title: en: Future: will and going to | ar: المستقبل: will وgoing to ¦ rule: en: Use 'be going to' for plans you have already made (I'm going to visit Rome) and for predictions from what you can see (Look at the clouds — it's going to rain). Use 'will' for decisions made now, promises and general predictions (I'll call you later). | ar: استخدم be going to للخطط المقرّرة مسبقًا (I'm going to visit Rome) وللتوقّع مما تراه (Look at the clouds — it's going to rain). واستخدم will للقرار اللحظي والوعود والتوقّعات العامة (I'll call you later). ¦ examples: We're going to move next month. = en: We're moving next month (already planned). | ar: سننتقل الشهر القادم (أمر مقرّر). / I'll help you with that. = en: A decision or offer made now. | ar: قرار أو عرض في اللحظة نفسها. / [marked incorrect] I will going to travel. = en: Use either 'will travel' or 'am going to travel' | ar: استخدم will travel أو am going to travel ¦ common_mistakes: en: ✗ I will to go → ✓ I will go (no 'to' after will). | ar: ✗ I will to go ← ✓ I will go (لا تأتي to بعد will).

title: en: First and second conditionals | ar: الجمل الشرطية الأولى والثانية ¦ rule: en: First conditional for real possibilities: If + present, will + verb (If it rains, we'll stay in). Second conditional for imaginary or unlikely situations: If + past, would + verb (If I had more time, I would learn Chinese). 'Unless' means 'if not'. | ar: الشرط الأول للاحتمالات الواقعية: If + مضارع، ثم will + فعل (If it rains, we'll stay in). والشرط الثاني للمواقف المتخيَّلة أو المستبعدة: If + ماضٍ، ثم would + فعل (If I had more time, I would learn Chinese). وunless تعني 'إذا لم'. ¦ examples: If you study, you'll pass. = en: A real possibility. | ar: احتمال واقعي. / If I were rich, I would travel the world. = en: An imaginary situation. | ar: موقف متخيَّل. / [marked incorrect] If it will rain, we stay home. = en: No 'will' in the if-clause | ar: لا تُستخدم will في جملة الشرط ¦ common_mistakes: en: ✗ If I would have money → ✓ If I had money. | ar: ✗ If I would have money ← ✓ If I had money.

title: en: Past continuous and past simple | ar: الماضي المستمر والماضي البسيط ¦ rule: en: Use was/were + -ing for an action in progress at a moment in the past (I was cooking at eight). Use the past simple for a shorter action that interrupts it: I was cooking when the phone rang. Use 'while' with two actions in progress at the same time. | ar: استخدم was/were + ‎-ing لفعل كان مستمرًا في لحظة من الماضي (I was cooking at eight). واستخدم الماضي البسيط لفعل أقصر قطعه: I was cooking when the phone rang. واستخدم while لفعلين مستمرين في الوقت نفسه. ¦ examples: I was walking home when it started to rain. = en: I was walking home when it started to rain. | ar: كنت أمشي إلى البيت عندما بدأ المطر. / While we were eating, the lights went out. = en: While we were eating, the lights went out. | ar: بينما كنا نأكل، انطفأت الأضواء. / [marked incorrect] I cooking dinner when the phone rang. = en: Use 'was cooking' | ar: استخدم was cooking ¦ common_mistakes: en: Verbs like know and want are rarely used with -ing: ✗ I was knowing → ✓ I knew. | ar: أفعال مثل know وwant نادرًا ما تأتي مع ‎-ing: ✗ I was knowing ← ✓ I knew.

title: en: should, must and have to | ar: should وmust وhave to ¦ rule: en: 'Should' gives advice (You should rest). 'Must' and 'have to' mean something is necessary; 'have to' is common for rules from outside (I have to wear a uniform). 'Mustn't' means it is not allowed, but 'don't have to' means it is not necessary. | ar: should للنصيحة (You should rest). وmust وhave to تعنيان أن الأمر ضروري، وhave to شائعة للقواعد المفروضة من الخارج (I have to wear a uniform). وmustn't تعني أن الأمر ممنوع، أما don't have to فتعني أنه غير ضروري. ¦ examples: You should drink more water. = en: You should drink more water. | ar: ينبغي أن تشرب ماء أكثر. / You don't have to come, but you can. = en: You don't have to come, but you can. | ar: لست مضطرًا إلى المجيء، لكن يمكنك ذلك. / [marked incorrect] You must to wear a helmet. = en: No 'to' after must | ar: لا تأتي to بعد must ¦ common_mistakes: en: Mixing up mustn't and don't have to: 'You mustn't pay' means paying is forbidden. | ar: الخلط بين mustn't وdon't have to: عبارة You mustn't pay تعني أن الدفع ممنوع.

title: en: Relative clauses: who, which, that, where | ar: جمل الصلة: who وwhich وthat وwhere ¦ rule: en: Use 'who' for people, 'which' for things and 'where' for places. 'That' can replace who or which in defining clauses: The man who/that lives next door is a doctor. You can leave out who/which/that when it is the object: The book (that) I read was great. | ar: استخدم who للأشخاص، وwhich للأشياء، وwhere للأماكن. ويمكن أن تحلّ that محل who أو which في جمل التعريف: The man who/that lives next door is a doctor. ويمكن حذف who/which/that حين تكون مفعولًا به: The book (that) I read was great. ¦ examples: She is the colleague who helped me. = en: She is the colleague who helped me. | ar: إنها الزميلة التي ساعدتني. / This is the café where we first met. = en: This is the café where we first met. | ar: هذا هو المقهى الذي التقينا فيه أول مرة. / [marked incorrect] The man which lives here is a doctor. = en: Use 'who' for people | ar: استخدم who للأشخاص ¦ common_mistakes: en: Repeating the object: ✗ the book that I read it → ✓ the book that I read. | ar: تكرار المفعول به: ✗ the book that I read it ← ✓ the book that I read.

title: en: The passive voice | ar: المبني للمجهول ¦ rule: en: Form the passive with be + past participle: Paper is made from wood; The bridge was built in 1990. Use it when the action matters more than who did it, or when we don't know who did it. Add 'by' to name the doer: It was painted by a local artist. | ar: يُصاغ المبني للمجهول بـ be + التصريف الثالث: Paper is made from wood؛ The bridge was built in 1990. ويُستخدم حين يهمّ الفعل أكثر من فاعله، أو حين لا نعرف الفاعل. وأضف by لذكر الفاعل: It was painted by a local artist. ¦ examples: This bread is baked every morning. = en: This bread is baked every morning. | ar: يُخبز هذا الخبز كل صباح. / The results were published last week. = en: The results were published last week. | ar: نُشرت النتائج الأسبوع الماضي. / [marked incorrect] The museum was build in 1900. = en: Use the past participle: built | ar: استخدم التصريف الثالث: built ¦ common_mistakes: en: Forgetting 'be': ✗ The letter sent yesterday → ✓ The letter was sent yesterday. | ar: نسيان be: ✗ The letter sent yesterday ← ✓ The letter was sent yesterday.

title: en: Reported speech | ar: الكلام المنقول ¦ rule: en: When we report what someone said, the verb usually moves one step back in time: "I'm tired" → She said (that) she was tired; "I will call" → He said he would call. Use 'say' without a person and 'tell' with a person: He told me he was busy. | ar: عند نقل كلام شخص يتراجع زمن الفعل عادةً خطوة إلى الماضي: "I'm tired" ← She said (that) she was tired؛ و"I will call" ← He said he would call. واستخدم say دون ذكر المخاطَب، وtell مع ذكره: He told me he was busy. ¦ examples: She said that she was hungry. = en: She said that she was hungry. | ar: قالت إنها جائعة. / He told me he would be late. = en: He told me he would be late. | ar: أخبرني أنه سيتأخر. / [marked incorrect] He said me that he was busy. = en: Use 'told me' or 'said that' | ar: استخدم told me أو said that ¦ common_mistakes: en: Reported questions use statement order: ✗ She asked where was the station → ✓ She asked where the station was. | ar: الأسئلة المنقولة تأخذ ترتيب الجملة الخبرية: ✗ She asked where was the station ← ✓ She asked where the station was.

title: en: Third conditional and wishes about the past | ar: الشرط الثالث والتمنّي في الماضي ¦ rule: en: Use the third conditional for imagined past situations that did not happen: If + had + past participle, would have + past participle (If I had left earlier, I would have caught the train). Use 'I wish' / 'If only' + had + past participle for regrets: I wish I had studied more. | ar: استخدم الشرط الثالث لمواقف متخيَّلة في الماضي لم تحدث: If + had + التصريف الثالث، ثم would have + التصريف الثالث (If I had left earlier, I would have caught the train). واستخدم I wish أو If only + had + التصريف الثالث للتعبير عن الندم: I wish I had studied more. ¦ examples: If you had told me, I would have helped. = en: If you had told me, I would have helped. | ar: لو أخبرتني لساعدتك. / I wish I hadn't said that. = en: I wish I hadn't said that. | ar: ليتني لم أقل ذلك. / [marked incorrect] If I would have known, I would have come. = en: Use 'had known' in the if-clause | ar: استخدم had known في جملة الشرط ¦ common_mistakes: en: ✗ If I had went → ✓ If I had gone (use the past participle). | ar: ✗ If I had went ← ✓ If I had gone (استخدم التصريف الثالث).

sentence: Nice to meet you ¦ meaning: en: Nice to meet you | ar: تشرّفت بمعرفتك
sentence: They ___ my brothers. ¦ accepted: are / 're

source: en: This is my mother. | ar: هذه أمي. ¦ accepted: This is my mother / This is my mom / This is my mum
